evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: ~11.69 mg/L at 46.0 h collapsing to 4.30 mg/L at 46.2 h and 2.62-2.74 mg/L by 51.4-52.0 h, vs source batches holding 10-11 mg/L at same ages
Receiving P assay: 2.449 g/L at t=48 h (available 52 h), lagging source-1/2/3 (~3.0, 3.02, 2.98 g/L)
Task constraint: minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0; downward trajectory projects violation within hours under KEEP
Forward model comparison at 52 h: strong_feed_reduction -> mass 148.5 kg, min DO 1.41 mg/L, deficit 1.67 mg·h/L, 1/5 feasible sensitivity members; best across all bounded actions
submission.rationale: At decision time 52 h the receiving fermentation shows a step-change oxygen crisis: DO2 dropped from ~11.7 mg/L at 46.0 h to ~4.3 mg/L at 46.2 h, and has continued eroding to 2.6-2.7 mg/L at 51.4-52.0 h — a drop-step not seen in any source batch (sources hold 9-11 mg/L at this age). DO2 is trending toward violation of the 2.0 mg/L minimum. KEEP alone is unacceptable. Among bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (0.6x feed + 1.15x air) is the most aggressive available response short of a stop (which would forfeit all counted production). The nominal source-calibrated forward model, while imperfect, consistently ranks it best: highest predicted product mass (~148.5 kg vs 138.8-140.4 kg for keep/combined), smallest post-decision oxygen deficit (1.67 mg·h/L vs 1.66-5.49 for other actions), and the lowest predicted below-limit exposure; it is also the only action whose parameter-sensitivity set includes feasible members. The dual mechanism (cut oxygen demand 40% and raise transfer 15%) directly addresses both possible causes of the crash (excess metabolic uptake after a feed-driven ramp and reduced transfer capacity), whereas air-only or feed-only options ranked worse on the same metrics.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is nominal and source-calibrated, not truth; even the chosen action is predicted infeasible at the nominal parameter point (min DO 1.41 mg/L, 5.2 h below limit) and only 1/5 sensitivity members is feasible, so the oxygen floor may still be breached despite intervention. Hidden receiving-process parameters (true OTR, OUR, feed trajectory) are unavailable. The cause of the DO step at 46.2 h (sensor fault vs real transfer drop) is not resolvable from public data; if the sensor is faulted, the intervention would cut feed unnecessarily and reduce production vs source trajectories. Assay values lag 4 h, so current product state is partially stale (latest P is t=48 h available at 52 h).

evidence: Receiving DO2 step drop from 11.69 mg/L (46.0 h) to 4.30 mg/L (46.2 h), unlike any source batch
DO2 decline continues to 2.74 mg/L at 52.0 h, approaching the 2.0 mg/L minimum with ~-0.05 mg/L/h slope
P assay at 48 h = 2.45 g/L (up from 0.99 g/L at 36 h): culture actively producing; stop or strong feed cut would sacrifice product mass
Source batches show self-recovering DO2 dips only with aeration step-ups (e.g., 24 h dip recovered after 28 h step-up); receiving 46 h event shows no recovery after 6 h
No evidence from KEEP trend that constraint violation will be avoided without intervention
submission.rationale: The receiving vessel suffered an abrupt oxygen-transfer deficit at ~46 h: DO2 fell from ~11.7 to ~4.3 mg/L in a single interval and has since declined monotonically to 2.74 mg/L at the 52 h decision point, on track to breach the 2.0 mg/L minimum within ~10-15 h. Product is still actively being produced (P: 0.99 g/L at 36 h to 2.45 g/L at 48 h), so retaining product mass rules out a stop or a severe feed cut. The combined bounded intervention (feed x0.8, air x1.15) reduces oxygen uptake demand while adding transfer headroom, addressing both sides of the OUR-vs-OTR imbalance and mirroring the aeration step-ups that restored DO2 in the source batches. Waiting for an extra assay is unnecessary: the DO2 sensor trend is unambiguous and time-critical.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden transfer and kinetic parameters are unavailable; the +15% air and -20% feed changes may not fully reverse the decline (if the deficit is larger than estimated) or may overshoot, slowing production more than needed. Sensor noise (~±0.2 mg/L) is small relative to the observed 9 mg/L step drop, so the deficit diagnosis is robust, but the post-intervention DO2 trajectory should be monitored and escalated (stronger reduction) if DO2 keeps falling below ~2.5 mg/L.
